clue.text: First half of song quietly managed by old singer

indicators.note: only the opening two of the four letters of the word song are kept

parts.note: the first two letters of song
P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A veteran vocalist gets through half a number softly, with someone else running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest voice range, so the answer is a type of vocalist.

clue.text: Sign of tailless arachnid

indicators.note: tailless means without its tail, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a scorpion is an arachnid, a relative of spiders

explanation.surface: An omen involving an eight-legged creature missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a scorpion without its sting; the wordplay just drops the last letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is a sign of the zodiac, represented by a scorpion.

clue.text: Bird of prey, unsettling for green pelican

indicators.note: unsettling means disturbing, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters of for green pelican, rearranged

explanation.surface: A hawk is disturbing for an inexperienced water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a raptor famed as the fastest diving bird.

clue.text: A good deal is needed for this call at whist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large quantity, plenty
second meaning: a bid in solo whist to win nine or more tricks

explanation.walkthrough: The middle words link the two meanings: an abundance call does need a good haul of tricks. Solo whist is a British card game in which players bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means plenty, and in solo whist it is the bid to take at least nine tricks.

clue.text: Ordinary blend handy

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for Ordinary, as in O level
to fuse is to blend or merge

explanation.surface: An everyday mixture that comes in useful.
explanation.walkthrough: O level was the Ordinary level school exam in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Of use means helpful or useful, the same as handy.

clue.text: Label associated with a southern company's sauce

parts.note: a tab is a small label or tag attached to something
CO is the abbreviation for company; the 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: A brand name linked to a firm from the south that makes a condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of company's is read as 'has' and links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a well-known hot pepper condiment from Louisiana, a trademarked chilli sauce.

clue.text: Student inside becoming keen on lecture

indicators.note: inside means the student letter goes within the phrase

parts.note: taking to means starting to like
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student gets keen on a lecture he is sitting in.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the learner plates on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding or reprimand, a stern lecture.

clue.text: Gallons aboard empty canal boat

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the gallons letter is put inside

parts.note: bare means empty, as in bare cupboards

explanation.surface: Fuel is loaded onto a narrowboat that was empty.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a flat-bottomed boat used on canals and rivers for carrying goods.

clue.text: Cast, home-grown, in new movie

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as a snake does its skin

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of home-grown, rearranged
the letters of in, rearranged

explanation.surface: A film cast entirely with local actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the film's actors but means SHED; 'new' rearranges HOMEGROWN IN into ONE HIM WRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: She Done Him Wrong is a 1933 film starring Mae West and Cary Grant.

clue.text: Elderly servant makes up simple card game

parts.note: old means elderly
a maid is a female servant

explanation.surface: An aged housemaid makes up a basic card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Maid is a children's card game in which players avoid being left with the odd queen.

clue.text: Novel, one we are both familiar with?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the title of a Charles Dickens novel

definitions.text: one we are both familiar with?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read literally, a friend known to both of us

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is the title read literally rather than as a book name.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Mutual Friend is Dickens's last completed novel, and the phrase literally describes an acquaintance shared by two people.

clue.text: Called Peru's leader well past his prime?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Peru

parts.note: first letter of Peru
aged means old, well past one's best years

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the head of a South American nation phoned in his dotage.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to summon them over a speaker system, so paged means summoned by call.

clue.text: Writer's strange email about Zoe Ball's latest broadcast

indicators.note: about means around, so the first rearranged set goes around the second
something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters of email are put in an unusual order

parts.note: the letters of email, rearranged

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its last one, here of Ball's

parts.note: last letter of Ball

explanation.surface: An odd message concerning the radio presenter Zoe Ball's most recent show.
explanation.walkthrough: Zoe Ball is a British radio and TV presenter; 'broadcast' looks like her show but is the second anagram signal, applying to Zoe alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola was a French novelist, author of Germinal; the 's stands for 'is' after the definition.

clue.text: Fried food item on one on part of stove?

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
a ring is a hob burner on a cooker

explanation.surface: Something fried is placed on top of one of the burners of a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion ring is a slice of onion battered and deep-fried, a common side order.

clue.text: Unsettled, head of institute approaches a bishop within

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of institute

indicators.note: within means the A and bishop letters go inside

parts.note: nears means approaches
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: An institute's director, troubled, nears a bishop inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In arrears means behind with payments, so the debts are still outstanding.

clue.text: Unpleasant ringing about money

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: bad means unpleasant
RE means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A nasty phone call concerning cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like a phone call but means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for cash, as is dough.

clue.text: Hibernate — when regenerated take some air?

indicators.note: regenerated means formed anew, so the letters are reformed into a different order

parts.note: the letters of Hibernate, rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal wakes from winter sleep and gets some fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe in is to inhale, drawing air into the lungs.

clue.text: Audibly quiet musical composition

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word for quiet is taken by its sound

parts.note: peace means quiet or calm

explanation.surface: A soft piece of music that can just be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a single work of music, such as a piano piece.

clue.text: Complete one's training in route through mountains abroad

parts.note: a pass is a way through a mountain range
out means outside, away from home

explanation.surface: Finishing a course with a trip through a foreign mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass out is to graduate from a military or police academy.

clue.text: Together, historically?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: simultaneously, all at the same moment
second meaning: formerly, in times past

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a phrase about a joint past, but each is a separate meaning of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both simultaneously, for things happening together, and formerly, for things once true in the past.

clue.text: European seabird on a lake unaffected by time

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A seabird from Europe sits on a lake, timeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, never changed by the passing years.

clue.text: Very thin person with ultimately needless worry about argument

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of needless is taken

parts.note: last letter of needless
care means worry or concern
C (circa) is the abbreviation for about
a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: A skinny man frets unnecessarily over a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarecrow is an informal term for a gaunt, ragged-looking person, like the figure in a field.

clue.text: Banishment from former French island

parts.note: ex means former
île is French for island

explanation.surface: Being sent away from a one-time French island.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is forced absence from one's homeland, the state of being sent away.

clue.text: Mineral springs in a cathedral city

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ..., a small cathedral city in Somerset, England

explanation.walkthrough: Wells is a small English city in Somerset, named after its springs.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells are sources of spring water, and Wells is also the smallest cathedral city in England.

clue.text: Redesigned seat fitted with wide strap

indicators.note: fitted with means having something put inside, so the second piece goes into the first
redesigned means given a new form, so the letters of seat are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of seat, rearranged
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A chair remodelled to include a broad belt.
explanation.walkthrough: A tawse is a Scottish leather strap formerly used to punish schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: A tawse is a leather belt with split ends, used for corporal punishment in Scottish schools.

clue.text: One Columbian, one travelling very rarely

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the letters of One Columbian, rearranged
the letters of one, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Colombian and another person seldom go on journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that happens extremely seldom, a blue moon being an uncommon event.

clue.text: Formal offers for small boats

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bids submitted for a contract
second meaning: boats that ferry people or supplies to a larger ship

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings sit side by side, joined by 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenders are formal bids for work, and also small craft serving a larger vessel.

clue.text: Country girl on French river I disregarded

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B places A after B
disregarded means ignored, so the letter I is dropped from the river

parts.note: the Seine flows through Paris
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A country girl beside a river in France who is ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: In a clue read across, 'on' means placed after, so the girl comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a nation in West Africa, on the Atlantic coast.
